lead: Gainesville plumbing deals with hard aquifer water, sinkhole-prone ground, college rentals and older homes. PipeMend sends licensed local plumbers across Gainesville.
risk: hard water scale, aging pipes in older homes and heavy use in student rentals
risk_short: hard water, old pipes and rentals
why: The Duckpond and areas near the University of Florida have homes from the 1900s to the 1950s with galvanized supply lines and cast-iron drains. Many homes near campus are rentals that see heavy use.
Gainesville sits on limestone with sinkholes in places, which can shift buried lines. Rare hard freezes burst exposed pipes.
water: GRU pumps water from the Floridan Aquifer and partly softens it. It is moderately hard at the tap. GRU also supplies natural gas and electricity.
tips: Give tenants a shutoff valve map.
Watch for new cracks or wet spots that could mean a shifted line.
Know where your gas shutoff is.
areas: PipeMend works in the Duckpond, the University of Florida area, Northwest Gainesville, Pleasant Street, Golfview and every other Gainesville neighborhood.
permits: Plumbing permits come from the City of Gainesville Building Inspections Division, and plumbing contractors are licensed by the Florida Construction Industry Licensing Board.

faq.q: Who supplies gas and water in Gainesville?
faq.a: Gainesville Regional Utilities runs water, natural gas and electric service. If you smell gas, leave the home and call 911 or GRU from outside.
